title: Rosalind and the Playlist
premise: In the dying mill town of Harrow Bend, Paloma Dunmore has survived high school by being invisible — until the ghost haunting Bellamy High starts leaving her handwritten notes in ink that shouldn't exist, each one naming a student who vanished decades ago. The notes lead her to a sealed 1974 fire report and a school board cover-up that traded six lives for insurance money. As the ghost's ink begins to fade — and with it, any chance of proof — Paloma must choose between protecting her found family from retaliation and telling a truth that could burn the town down. In the end she publishes everything, the board falls, and the ghost is finally named and mourned: not a monster, but a girl who stayed behind because no one would say her name.
about_author: F. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering school board meetings no one attended. They write young adult fiction about kids who refuse to look away.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Establishes her careful invisibility in Harrow Bend: head down, grades up, one safe table at lunch with her two friends. The chapter ends when she opens her locker to find a note addressed 'Paloma' in ink that shimmers like it's still wet. Beat: unease cracking routine.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She researches the school's legendary ghost, said to haunt the old east wing. A 1974 yearbook shows six senior photos with names scratched out. Her best friend Dez thinks it's a prank; her other friend Marisol begs her to drop it. Beat: curiosity vs. self-preservation.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A second note appears inside her locked house, listing dates and a name: Wren Alcott. Testing the ink, she finds it's warm, smells of smoke, and vanishes under UV light. Someone — or something — knows things no living person should. Beat: dread deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: East Wing Rules
chapters.summary: Paloma and Dez sneak into the condemned east wing after hours. Cold spots, a scorched classroom door, and chalk writing that reads STAY OUT OF THE BASEMENT. They flee when footsteps follow them out. Beat: first real danger, thrill and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Marisol Knows Something
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Revealed: her grandmother was a secretary at Bellamy in 1974 and made Marisol promise never to ask about the fire. Marisol has been quietly destroying clues for years to protect her family. Beat: loyalty revealed as its own kind of burden.

chapters.title: The Sealed Report
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the ghost's clues, she finds the original fire inspection report hidden in the library's archive cage — six students were locked in during a 'drill.' The official record says five died and one transferred. Beat: the cover-up takes shape.

chapters.title: Board of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma attends a school board meeting and asks about the 1974 fire. Chairman Hollis Vann shuts her down with practiced charm; afterward, an anonymous adult warns her to stop. Her mother gets a threatening call about Paloma's 'obsessions.' Beat: the machinery of power flexing.

chapters.title: What Dez Carries
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez confesses their older cousin was paid off years ago after asking questions, and that Dez has been helping Paloma partly to finish what family started. First kiss between Dez and Paloma, immediately shadowed by fear. Beat: found family solidifying under pressure.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The ghost finally manifests: a girl in a 1970s letterman jacket, translucent, fading at the edges. Wren can't leave the building and can only write while her ink lasts. She shows Paloma the basement door where the sixth student — the one who 'transferred' — actually escaped and never spoke. Beat: grief meets urgency.

chapters.title: The Sixth Survivor
chapters.summary: Paloma and Marisol track the survivor to a nursing home two counties away. He confirms everything but refuses to go on record: Vann's father led the cover-up, and the town's economy depended on the insurance payout. Beat: truth without witnesses is almost worthless.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her locker is vandalized with slurs; someone reports her family to child services on false grounds. Marisol's grandmother's records are stolen from the historical society. The message is clear: stop, or everyone you love pays. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Cornered between her grandmother's promise and her friends, Marisol admits what she's been hiding. Paloma feels betrayed; Dez tries to mediate. The trio splits just as they need each other most. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turned inward.

chapters.title: Fading
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wren is nearly transparent now; her notes come in broken half-words. She gives Paloma her last full message: the location of the physical evidence — the actual padlocked drill log — hidden in the basement. Time limit established. Beat: ticking clock made flesh.

chapters.title: The Basement Door
chapters.summary: Paloma and Dez break into the basement at night and find the drill log proving students were deliberately locked in. But Vann is waiting — he's known about the ghost for years and has been managing the legend his whole career. Beat: trap sprung.

chapters.title: Bargain
chapters.summary: Vann offers Paloma a scholarship, her mother's job security, and silence in exchange for the log. He reveals he let the ghost story grow because a haunted school kept reporters away better than any lock. Beat: temptation articulated — survival offered at the cost of Wren's name.

chapters.title: Ashes and Answers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, refusing the deal. Vann burns the log in front of her — but Paloma already photographed every page, and Marisol arrives with her grandmother's hidden carbon copies. Reconciliation: Marisol chose them. Beat: the trio reunited, evidence secured.

chapters.title: Going Loud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven over one week. The trio distributes copies to the county paper, a state journalist, and every household mailbox in Harrow Bend. The town splits; some parents thank them, others spit. Vann suspends all three. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the emergency board hearing, the sixth survivor arrives in a wheelchair to testify, ending fifty years of silence. Wren appears briefly in the doorway — visible, for one moment, to everyone in the room. Beat: public climax; the dead given witness.

chapters.title: Naming the Dead
chapters.summary: The board resigns en masse as the state investigation opens. Paloma leads a memorial assembly where all six names are read aloud for the first time, Wren Alcott last. The east wing's cold spots go quiet mid-ceremony. Beat: catharsis; the ghost released by remembrance.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Small victories and costs: the suspension reversed, but some friendships in town permanently burned. Dez and Paloma navigate being openly together in a town learning to look at itself. Beat: tenderness after rupture.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Final visit to the empty east wing before demolition. She finds one last note in ordinary, human ink: THANK YOU FOR SAYING MY NAME — signed Wren. Whether it was the ghost or a living hand, Paloma chooses to believe. Beat: bittersweet closure.

chapters.title: Playlist for the Living
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. One year later: a memorial garden, a scholarship in Wren's name, and Paloma leaving for college with a mixtape from Dez. She's done being invisible — but now visibility is a choice, not a sentence. Final beat: survival redefined as living out loud.
